item.title: Controversy arises on Facebook following comments by Augusta DA

item.title: Indie fantasy drama filmed in Augusta to premiere at Sacred Heart Cultural Center
item.description: Gary Mazeffa, the writer and director of the film “Asherah: A Love Odyssey,” recalled when years ago he would jest with people in public, facetiously responding to common, polite offers of assistance—such as a store clerk asking, “is there anything I can do for you?”—with “What’s the meaning of life?” The post Indie fantasy drama filmed in Augusta to premiere at Sacred Heart Cultural Center appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: RCSS holds third public hearing on Facilities Master Plan ahead of Feb. 23 vote
item.description: Richmond County School System leaders held their third public hearing Thursday on the district's proposed 2026 Long-Range Facilities Master Plan, giving community members one final opportunity to voice concerns before the Board of Education votes on Feb. 23. The post RCSS holds third public hearing on Facilities Master Plan ahead of Feb. 23 vote appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Candidates continue to announce plans to run for local office in Columbia County
item.description: While qualifying for the May 19 primary doesn’t take place until next month, several people have announced their intentions to run for office. The post Candidates continue to announce plans to run for local office in Columbia County appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: ASMP inmate formally charged in January stabbing death in Columbia County
item.description: Authorities have arrested and charged a 25-year-old inmate with murder in the Jan. 20 stabbing death of fellow inmate Jerry W. Merritt at Augusta State Medical Prison. item.title: Burger King employee hit with new charges for pulling gun & making threats
item.description: The man at the center of a Burger King feud involving a gun and several employees has now been charged with more serious offenses and denied bond. The Richmond County Sheriff’s Office says the trouble began around 5:34 p.m. on Jan. 22 at the Burger King on Deans Bridge Road in Augusta.
